raw.details:
Download Problem Statements from our website and get more details:

https://www.sdg-hackathon.in/

Build AI that solves real problems.

This hackathon is organized by the ACM Student Chapter at BV(DU) College of Engineering, Pune (Department of Computer Science & Engineering). Students are invited to build practical, responsible AI solutions for real-world problems connected to the UN's Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).

How It Works

  • Register your team and pick one main problem area (SDG track).
  • Submit your idea online (a short slide deck).
  • Reviewers screen all ideas remotely.
  • Top teams are shortlisted and invited to Pune.
  • Selected teams attend an online briefing, then come onsite for 2 days to build, test, and present their project.
  • Final pitches, judging, and prize distribution happen on the last day.

Important Dates

  • Last date to register and submit idea: 20 Sep 2026, 11:59 PM
  • Online screening: 21–22 Sep
  • Results (finalists announced): 23 Sep (top 20 teams)
  • Online oreintation for finalists: 25 Sep, 6 PM
  • Onsite hackathon: 26–27 Sep, 11 AM–7 PM (both days)
  • Final presentations and awards: 27 Sep, by 7 PM

Note: This is NOT an overnight/48-hour hackathon. No overnight stay is needed or allowed. You go home each evening.

Choose a Problem Area
Pick one topic to focus on: Hunger, Health, Education, Gender Equality, Clean Water, Clean Energy, Jobs & Economy, Infrastructure, Reducing Inequality, Smart Cities, Responsible Consumption, Climate Change, Ocean Life, Land & Nature, or Justice & Good Governance. Each topic has specific real-world challenges listed on the website with challenge IDs — pick one and quote it in your submission.

What to Submit First (Round 1)
A short presentation (5–7 slides, PPT or PDF) that covers:

  • The problem you're solving and who it affects
  • Which SDG goal it connects to
  • Your proposed solution and how it works
  • How AI actually helps (not just AI for the sake of it)
  • Your technical plan (data, models, tools, possible risks)
  • Expected impact and your team's roles

Onsite Finale Schedule

  • Day 1 (26 Sep): Reporting and opening brief, build begins, lunch break, mentor check-in, progress review, day ends by 7 PM
  • Day 2 (27 Sep): Build continues with mentor support, lunch break, final code submission, judges review projects, top teams present, prizes and closing ceremony

Prizes — Total Rs. 15,000 (funded by ACM India)

  • 1st Place: Rs. 8,000
  • 2nd Place: Rs. 5,000
  • 3rd Place: Rs. 2,000
  • Extra sponsor prizes may be added later

How You'll Be Judged (out of 100 points)

  • Real-world impact – 25 points
  • How well it works (technical build) – 25 points
  • Creativity – 15 points
  • Safe and responsible use of AI – 15 points
  • Practicality (can it actually be used?) – 10 points
  • How well you explain and demo it – 10 points

Rules to Keep It Fair

  • If you reuse any code, data, AI models, or prompts, you must clearly mention it.
  • Explain where your data comes from and how you're keeping AI use safe and responsible.
  • Your final submission should include a working prototype, code repository, slide deck, and demo.
  • Be respectful, follow campus rules, and respect others' intellectual property.
  • You can use AI tools and open-source code, but must disclose them.
  • Your team keeps ownership of your original work (though third-party tools/data follow their own rules).

Who Can Join

  • Any student currently enrolled in a recognized college or university
  • Team size: 2 to 4 members
  • All members must be 18+ on the day of registration (if someone is under 18, contact the organizers beforehand for guardian consent)

Registration Fee
Rs. 100, one-time, per team (not per person).

What You Get at the Venue
Wi-Fi, power, seating/workspace, food and refreshments, mentor support, jury feedback, and certificates for eligible finalists.

What You Should Bring
Laptop, charger, valid college ID, any datasets/API keys you plan to use, personal essentials, and a demo-ready prototype by Day 2.

Other Things to Know

  • Travel and accommodation are not provided or reimbursed by the organizers.
